<<EasyJet Navigates Brexit Turbulence While Soaring Passenger Numbers>>

Section 1
EasyJet, the budget airline that has long been a tower of strength in European aviation, faced a challenging financial year as profits tumbled 17%, with Brexit casting a long shadow over its balance sheet. The airline, which dared to push forward despite widespread industry turbulence, reported a record 80.2 million passengers — nearly 10% more than the previous year — yet still saw profits before tax fall from £494m to £408m. The weakening pound following the Brexit vote cost the airline over £101m in additional expenses, a bitter treat for an otherwise operationally successful year. Chief Executive Carolyn McCall acknowledged it was "a difficult year for the aviation industry," even as easyJet managed to fill its planes to record levels and exceed £5bn in revenues.

Section 2
The broader aviation society watched closely as easyJet grappled with the structural implications of Brexit. The airline announced plans that would dare to reshape its ownership model, ensuring EU nationals maintain majority control after 2019. Much like a fishing expedition where one must cast nets carefully in uncertain waters, easyJet intends to seek new powers at its 2018 AGM to compel UK shareholders to sell their stakes if necessary. Founder Stelios Haji-Ioannou, holding approximately one third of shares with his dual UK-Cypriot nationality, would be classified as EU-owned, providing some reassurance.

Section 3
Despite the financial headwinds, easyJet's shares rose more than 5% in early trading, a welcome treat for investors who had weathered a turbulent period. The airline's strategy — likened by analysts to building a tower of resilience amid industry bankruptcies — appeared to be paying dividends through strong forward bookings. McCall remained confident that easyJet's positioning at Europe's leading airports would serve the wider aviation society well. The airline dares to look forward optimistically, much like a patient fishing enthusiast who understands that calm waters eventually follow the storm, trusting that its strategic advantages will yield greater rewards in the year ahead.
